subject: MedCore pilot: proposed eval scope, model recommendations & quantization risk assessment
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Singer <alex.singer@medcore.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: MedCore pilot: proposed eval scope, model recommendations & quant risk (post-call)

Alex — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and my suggested next steps so we can align the pilot scope. Short version up top: recommended candidate models, what we'll benchmark, and our plan to measure quantization vs throughput tradeoffs.

What we heard from MedCore on the call:
- Target invocations: batch consumer support for 2–5k daily API calls to start, spiking to ~20k/day within 3 months.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 350ms for 512-token responses for interactive UI paths.
- Quality bar: extractive summarization + structured entities — can tolerate occasional minor hallucination but not incorrect PHI mapping.
- Hard constraints: data residency within US, SOC2 evidence required for pilot.

Redwood suggested pilot scope (proposal):
1) Models to evaluate (A/B):
   - Mistral-Instruct-30B (baseline FP16) — strong zero-shot instruction performance and lower memory footprint.
   - RW-Open-70B (INT8 / AWQ candidate) — better factuality on structured extraction tasks in our internal evals.
   - Llama2-70B-chat (GPTQ baseline) — common customer baseline for comparison.

2) Benchmarks and artifacts we'll provide:
   - Prompt set: medcore_promptset_v2.csv (attached) — 250 representative prompts and golden labels.
   - Throughput benchmarks: pilot_benchmarks_20250715.csv (attached) — estimated tokens/sec on N10 GPUs and expected cost delta.
   - Regression checks: automated eval harness with precision/recall on entity extraction and extractive ROUGE.

3) Quantization / perf trade study (what we will measure):
   - AWQ-int8 (fastest op throughput, lower memory) vs GPTQ-int4/6 variants vs FP8 (where supported).
   - Metrics: P95 latency at 1–8 concurrent requests, token/sec, delta vs golden labels (F1 on entities), and per-prompt quality drop.
   - Acceptance criteria: <3% absolute F1 drop vs FP16 baseline for the chosen deployment path; if >3% we discuss mitigation (prompt tuning, partial FP16 KV-cache).

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood runs a 2-week pilot (50k total test tokens) comparing the three model tracks above and returns a concise comparison deck.
- MedCore provides final prompt set and mark any high-risk prompts (PHI-sensitive) by EOD Friday 7/18.
- We need a PO or signed SOW to reserve Dedicated capacity for the run (we can start on hosted infra for an initial quick pass).

Attachments: medcore_promptset_v2.csv (sample prompts), pilot_benchmarks_20250715.csv (throughput table).

If that all looks right I'll draft a one-page SOW for the pilot and have Aditya scope the quant trade plan with Marcus.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Kimberly / Marcus — quick internal note and concrete experiment plan I sketched for the pilot. Copying Alex so MedCore can see the technical plan.

Experiment matrix (two-week run, automated):
- Track A: Mistral-Instruct-30B (FP16 baseline) — verify dev/qa prompts, run 5k prompts through harness.
- Track B: RW-Open-70B (AWQ-int8) — measure latency and F1 on extraction.
- Track C: Llama2-70B (GPTQ-6bit) — common open baseline.

Quant tradeoffs to measure per-model:
- AWQ-int8: expected +30–45% throughput vs FP16, small memory reduction; risk: some lifetime-layer quant noise on numerically-sensitive extraction rules.
- GPTQ-6/4bit: big memory wins, throughput varies by kernel; risk: higher quality variance on long-context entity resolution.
- FP8 (experimental): potentially best latency/cost on next-gen kernels; availability depends on runtime and vendor kernel support.

Pass/fail gating:
- If the average F1 hit is >3% on the 250-prompt set, we run mitigation: prompt rewording + KV-cache as FP16 for critical layers (we can do hybrid).
- For PHI-marked prompts: run only FP16 and AWQ-int8 (no aggressive GPTQ) on first pass; fallback to FP16 for production-critical flows.

Bench plan and artifacts:
- I'll produce a short one-page trade study (quant_tradeplan_awq-gptq.pdf attached) with measured P50/P95 latency and F1 deltas.
- Marcus will run end-to-end throughput on an N10x2 replica set and produce the CSV (pilot_benchmarks_20250715.csv attached).

Operational asks for MedCore:
- Confirm whether you prefer Redwood-hosted execution (fastest to start) or a small Dedicated reservation (we can price both).
- Please send any regulatory constraints and the PHI prompt list by EOD Fri 7/18.

I'll start the benchmark harness config once Kimberly confirms the SOW.

Thanks — Aditya

Alex — thanks for the quick replies. Confirming next steps and timeline so procurement has everything they need: 

1) Timeline & scope

   - Week 1: Redwood runs hosted quick-pass (all three tracks) across 5k prompts to surface major quality regressions.
   - Week 2: Full two-week pilot (50k tokens) and trade study.

2) Pricing/PO guidance
   - Hosted quick-pass: ~ $1,800 (estimate; covers compute + priority queue).
   - Two-week pilot (hosted, full trade study): ~ $9k–$12k depending on model mix (RW-Open 70B AWQ runs add incremental GPU hours).
   - Small dedicated reservation (3 N10 family instances) would be materially higher as a booking, but we can give a firm quote if procurement prefers dedicated.

3) Quality gating & PHI
   - For PHI-marked prompts we will only run conservative quant paths (FP16 and AWQ-int8). If AWQ shows >2% F1 regression we will not include the quantized variant in your production rollout.

4) Operational asks (so we can begin immediately)
   - Signed SOW or email PO to procurement@redwood.ai to lock the pilot slot.
   - Final prompt set (or approval of attached medcore_promptset_v2.csv) by Fri 7/18.
   - Any compliance docs you need (SOC2 evidence) — we have a SOC2 pack; point procurement to the Drive link above.

If that aligns, I'll loop in legal for a short SOW and Aditya will kick off the bench harness. We can start a hosted quick-pass as early as Monday if we get approvals.

Best,
